sites.functional_impact_measured: Living neurons expressing NF186 K519TAG were labeled with ATTO488-tz before fixation and immunostained with anti-HA and anti-ankG antibodies, confirming surface display of the tagged full-length NF186 at the AIS. Full-length protein confirmed by Western blot with anti-HA.
sites.rationale: L5 (grounded in L1/L3) reports site-specific UAA incorporation at K519 of full-length rat NF186, with surface labeling confirmed in living neurons. Human NFASC position 519 is K (identical to rat), so the numbering transfers directly. The UAA is incorporated AT K519, making insert_after_residue=518 (V) with residue_after=K(519). This is a validated extracellular position with confirmed surface accessibility, qualifying as tolerance of a different (chemical) insertion modality. NF186 K519TAG: amber stop codon introduced at K519 of rat Nfasc gene in full-length membrane-anchored NF186. Unnatural amino acid (UAA) incorporated at position 519 via PylRS-AF/tRNA-Pyl system, then labeled with ATTO488-tz by click chemistry in living neurons. Human position 519 is K (identical to rat).

Note: human NFASC position 534 is R (arginine), not K; rat has K534 at this position — species difference at this single residue.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: HA-NF186-GFP targeted to the paranodal segment of DRG neurons and colocalized with ankyrin G (rhodamine), confirming correct surface display and subcellular localization.
sites.rationale: L8 reports HA-NF186-GFP with an N-terminal HA tag on full-length membrane-anchored NF186. With signal peptide spanning residues 1-24, the N-terminal tag must be placed after the SP cleavage site (after residue 24, A) and before the first mature residue (25, I). The topology is unambiguous: NF186 is a type I TM protein with a single extracellular N-terminus, so the N-terminal tag position is topology-derived. The construct was confirmed to reach the cell surface and localize correctly to the paranodal segment. HA-NF186-GFP: full-length NF186 with N-terminal HA tag and C-terminal GFP expressed in DRG neurons. The HA tag is placed after the signal peptide (residues 1-24) and before the mature extracellular domain (residue 25 onward). The protein is membrane-anchored with a single TM domain (1218-1238).

sources.claim: (middle) HA-NF186-GFP is targeted to the PS (arrows) of DRG neurons, where it colocalizes with ankyrin G (rhodamine).

literature_notes: L2 (C-terminal HA on NF186) and L6 (C-terminal FLAG on Nfasc155) and L7 (FLAG-Nfasc186 at nodes) all place tags at the intracellular C-terminus (after TM domain 1218-1238), so they are recorded in other_positions. L9 (NF-TurboID chimeric fusion) does not specify a junction residue or named loop in the ledger clip, so no site can be pinned from it. The six UAA/click-chemistry sites (K519, K534, K571, K604, K680, K809) from PMC10323244 are classified as 'published tolerance of a different insertion' because UAA incorporation is a single-residue chemical labeling modality analogous to AviTag/tetracysteine rather than a peptide-tag insertion; however, surface display was directly confirmed by live-cell ATTO488-tz labeling (L5), making these strong evidence for extracellular accessibility. For K534, human NFASC has R at position 534 (rat has K); the position is conserved but the residue differs, lowering confidence for that site. The N-terminal HA site (L8) is topology-derived: with signal peptide 1-24, the only extracellular N-terminus is after residue 24, and the paper names no specific residue number.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on NF186 (CMV-NF186 WT-HA); C-terminus is intracellular (after TM 1218-1238), not a surface site.
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length Nfasc155 in transgenic mice; C-terminus is intracellular, not a surface site.
FLAG-tagged Nfasc186 rescues nodal components; FLAG tag is at C-terminus (intracellular) based on L6 context from the same paper.
